I uninstalled it after finding basic terminal functions broken... they've hijacked the 'clear' command... it only works when run separately instead of as part of a sequence.
I'm a Warp fanboy... Warp is magic for linux sys admin. I SSH into my home server and feel like a wizard, no more constantly switching to a web browser to Google stuff.
Warp must be hemorrhaging all of their cash if they stoop so low as to try to scam developers. Bye bye, Warp. Trash product. Trash leadership.
I tried Warp once... it showed me a login prompt. Perhaps I mistakenly downloaded a login prompt app instead of a terminal app? I promptly uninstalled it.
I remember seeing this terminal emulator, deciding to give it a shot, and being asked to sign in. I have never uninstalled a program faster in my life.

Warp co-founder: fair criticism, and this is the reason we removed the login requirement... the point of the login is that we have features that cost money to provide like AI and collaboration, not anything more nefarious.
Warp is great - I use it as my daily terminal. The best features are being able to edit commands, chunking the output into blocks and AI generated commands at your fingertips.
My daily driver for a few months now, even after trying Rio/Ghostty/Wezterm... Favorite feature is the notification when a long running command has finished.

Warp is so horribly broken right now and has been for weeks. Multiple github issues on consistent issue writing file. On top of that UI glitches, and inability to use the code indexing feature, file and diff Explorer while in WSL or any ssh connection. It's practically unusable.
I've been a Pro user for several months (use < 1000 credits a month) - but I've noticed a real reduction in quality over the past month or so. I'm now getting random failures, stopping of agents etc.
Warp is a terrible product, and I have nothing nice to say about them. But look at modern terminals like Kitty or Ghostty... mouse support that works well, fast keyboard response.
I installed this, lasted about 90 seconds on my machine before I went back to iTerm.

Nearly everything about the experience of a terminal is better than iTerm though? Very nice having the terminal treated like a text file. It has issues with ssh'ing into one machine but I just use command ssh for that single machine.
Their terminal is just Alacritty... The terminal emulator was never their selling point, the AI wrapper was.
They have also innovated by requiring login (into a console!!)... Today they have heaps of telemetry, so a privacy nightmare. This is a terminal that is not designed for users.
Warp is a masterclass in how to have a great product statement, very nice UI and completely ruin it with greed, closed-source, and by not listening to your customers.
